I was a member of WOTSO in Australia before I moved to NZ.

I thought I'd continue here, and did a few trial days here when I first arrived. It is now a month on and I am was about to sign the lease for a place nearby so I can work out of the office.

I do not think the reception was authorised to send the email. I believe HR is covering for them when they have acted wrongly. I believe HR is lying to me about a previous report they'd had.

HR refuses to elaborate. I am deeply troubled by this series of events. I am confident this is not some prejudical thing, as frankly I do not fit the profile. All the same, it deeply troubles me to think I am less then welcome somewhere in my new City.

I loved WOTSO in Australia. I was a member of the Manly location. I cannot recommend it enough if you make the switch! The management there is just lovely.

I am not sure why you have excluded me, however I want you to know this is more than just an inconvenience. I had made a large assumption about the availability of your space. I did not think inclusivity would be an issue.

I've never written a bad review before and I wasn't going to write this, but yesterday I (coincidentally) talked to somebody who'd been given the same runaround when she went to get her scooter repaired, so here goes.

I have never dealt with anybody as unprofessional as Mike. Communication was almost nil and I shouldn't have had to hound *him* for updates, but I did. I also realise that my scooter needed parts ordered internationally - that's going to take a bit of time and I accept that. But having worked in freight, ordered things internationally and having a rough idea of how long these things take, my scooter was in the shop at least twice as long as it needed to be.

When I did (occasionally) hear back from Mike, it was usually along the lines of "I'm going to Auckland... won't be back until XYZ date!" That happened about two or three times. Fast forward to today... my scooter has been in the shop for over TWO months and although Mike is in Auckland (again), he says his mate will come by and open up the shop.

At first it was 12:30. Then change of plans... 11:30. Then "His flight is running late so it's 1:15!" I have to blow off an afternoon shift to make it (which I was not thrilled about), but I just wanted it all to be over. After about 20 plus minutes of waiting, another text from Mike saying "His flight was delayed... he'll be there soon!"

While I was waiting I had a bit of a talk with one of the people from one of the other shops in the complex. He told me he'd seen a *lot* of people waiting outside Mike's shop like I was and they all seemed very frustrated and unhappy.

Eventually Mike's mate pulls up... very nervous looking fellow. I get the feeling he's the one who usually has to deal with unhappy customers while Mike is off jetsetting wherever and I kinda feel sorry for him. Thankfully I was able to get my scooter back (two months or so later), pay the agreed upon amount and finally be done with an infuriating, frustrating ordeal.

Long story short, I have NEVER dealt with anybody so unprofessional in my life! At many points I felt like I was being scammed and if I hadn't got my scooter back today, I was seriously considering going to the police. It's a disgusting, disrespectful and unprofessional way to run a business and if I knew the whole ordeal was going to be like pulling teeth, I would have gone literally anywhere else.

I will NEVER deal with Mike again and unless you enjoy having your time wasted, having to hound somebody for updates, getting blown off and dealing with excuse after excuse, I would strongly advise going literally anywhere else. I am coeliac and ordered one of the sandwiches, which I specifically requested gluten free for. The waiter brought out the sandwich and advised it was the gluten free one. More than 5 minutes later, after I had already finished the first half of the sandwich, another sandwich was brought out and I was advised that the one I had eaten was actually not the gluten free sandwich and that that waiter had made an error. The waiter himself was apologetic and understandably unsure of how to fix the error given it was only his first day on the job. However, it was the service from more senior staff that followed that made this experience terrible.

The staff were not at all apologetic and clearly did not understand the severity of the mistake, even when I explained I am allergic to gluten and this would make me extremely unwell. I then explained that we would need to leave the restaurant to go home before I became unwell and we requested for any remaining food to be packed up, along with a refund for the sandwich, given the harm they have caused from providing unsafe food. The staff rolled their eyes and said “oh but you have your sandwich now”. Eventually after multiple requests, the staff agreed to a $25 refund, however, it was disappointing that this was not offered by the staff initially. Following this, my friend advised they were still waiting for their sandwich to be packed up and the staff advised this was missing off the bill, even though they ordered it. Very disappointing customer service at Big Barrel Otahuhu today.

I purchased a carton of Steinlager and carried it straight out to my car. I had not dropped the carton or even placed it down when I heard a slight clink from inside. When I checked, I found that one of the bottles had broken inside the carton.

I went straight back into the store, not demanding a refund or accusing anyone, but simply asking whether the bottle could possibly have already been damaged or cracked. Beer bottles are fairly sturdy, so I thought it was reasonable to ask.

Instead of listening or even checking the carton, the person at the counter immediately responded along the lines of, “You did it.”

He then called another staff member from the back. What disappointed me most was this person's attitude. In a very unpleasant and dismissive tone, he told me to take the carton because I had damaged it myself, while making a hand gesture for me to leave.

At that point I did raise my voice slightly because I was frustrated by the way I was being spoken to. I told him that his customer service was poor and that he needed to learn how to speak to customers respectfully.

I understand that the store may not have been willing to replace the broken bottle if they believed the damage happened after purchase. I can accept that. What I cannot accept is being immediately blamed and dismissed without anyone even taking the time to listen or inspect what had happened.

A simple, respectful explanation such as, “Sorry, unfortunately once the carton has left the store we can't replace damaged bottles,” would have been completely understandable.

The issue wasn't the cost of one bottle. It was the attitude and the way a paying customer was treated.

Very disappointing experience and definitely not the level of customer service I would expect.
